node-1.label: Patient exhibits progressively more violent dream enactment behavior during sleep

node-2.label: Patient is a man in his late 60s with a 15-year history of Parkinson disease (Hoehn and Yahr score, 3) and a 20-year history of sleep disturbance

node-3.label: Daytime motor symptoms improved after deep brain stimulation, but dream enactment episodes became progressively more violent, including assaulting his wife and self-injurious behaviors

node-4.label: Yelling occurred multiple times per night; violent behaviors such as punching through walls or striking furniture were reported every other night

node-5.label: Despite removing all objects from the bedroom and placing the mattress on the floor, the patient continued to strike walls and the ground, causing self-injury and property damage; one severe episode caused a head laceration requiring emergency department evaluation

why.why: Radiologist analysis independently concludes the clinical presentation is highly consistent with Parkinson-associated RBD, citing the long-standing Parkinson disease history and classic violent dream-enactment parasomnia; the sleep-related injury pattern and absence of psychiatric evidence further support this diagnosis. The only limitation is that polysomnography and medication/DBS parameter results remain pending, so objective confirmation of REM sleep without atonia is not yet available; this raises confidence from 0.8 to 0.87.

Radiologist analysis acknowledges that deep brain stimulation may have exacerbated the episodes but classifies it as a contributing factor rather than the primary cause, consistent with the temporal relationship in the history. Thus the hypothesis that DBS contributed to exacerbation remains plausible but secondary, with confidence unchanged at 0.25.

Radiologist analysis explicitly excludes a primary psychiatric/behavioral disorder based on the sleep-related injury pattern and absence of psychiatric evidence; the violent behaviors occur in the context of REM sleep parasomnia rather than voluntary behavior. Confidence is reduced from 0.05 to 0.02.
